newsitem.title: USA: Union pilots ask American to accept proposal.
newsitem.headline: Union pilots ask American to accept proposal.

text.p: Union pilots at American Airlines appealed to the carrier Friday to accept its "modest proposal" to avert the threat of a strike set for midnight.
James Sovich, president of the Allied Pilots Association, said in a statement "I appeal to AMR Corp (the parent of American Airlines) to do the right thing."
Sovich said in remarks prepared for a press conference that "I very much hope that management chooses the prudent course, rather than forcing our pilots to strike."
His remarks followed more than four days of round-the-clock bargaining and only hours before the union has pledged to strike if no deal is reached.
He said that pilots have not had a pay increase since negotiations began three years ago and that asking for a pay increase of a total of 11 percent through the year 2000 was a reasonable settlement.

He said that "I cannot conceive of any valid reason why our pilots should see their wages decline in real terms and why they should have to be concerned about the potential out-sourcing of their jobs."
He was referring to union concerns about American's plan to buy small jets for its commuter airlines, American Eagle, and use lower-paid pilots to fly them.
American has said that it needed small jets flown by lower-paid pilots to compete with other major airlines who are operating low-cost commuter services.
